feeds.title: Speaking of Art Blog
feeds.description: Mary Ann Pals is a pastel and charcoal artist living near the southern tip of Lake Michigan in Chesterton, IN. She has enjoyed doing artwork all her life. In college, she received her degree in Humanities with an emphasis in the Visual Arts.

feeds.title: Arts Council of Southwestern Indiana
feeds.description: The Arts Council of Southwestern Indiana is a nonprofit arts organization formed in 1970. For more than 50 years the Arts Council has worked hard at fulfilling its mission of enhancing the quality of life in the region and bolstering economic development by advocating and promoting arts, arts education, and arts organizations in southwestern Indiana.

feeds.title: Visit Columbus » Arts and Culture
feeds.description: The Visitors Center includes a gift shop, as well as the Yellow Neon Chandelier and Persians by glass artist Dale Chihuly, and serves as the starting point for tours, which feature architecture, public art, the Miller House and Garden, and landmarks.

feeds.title: Fort Wayne Museum of Art Blog
feeds.description: The Fort Wayne Museum of Art leverages the power of art to engage and educate broad and diverse audiences throughout Northeast Indiana.

feeds.title: Fishers Arts Council Blog
feeds.description: The Fishers Arts Council is a prominent arts organization in Fishers, Indiana. Our mission is to support, advocate, and cultivate visual and performing arts opportunities that educate, enhance, and enrich the lives of those who live, work, and visit Fishers. We collaborate with local organizations, artists, performers, students, and others to create vibrant arts and culture occasions in our city.

feeds.title: Indianapolis Business Journal » Arts & Entertainment
feeds.description: Indianapolis Business IBJ.com and Indianapolis Business Journal are central Indiana's business authority. IBJ (Indianapolis Business Journal) is a reliable source for business news and financial information in central Indiana and Indianapolis. It provides breaking news and in-depth coverage across various domains, including real estate, health care, sports business, small business, and arts & entertainment.

feeds.title: Indianapolis Recorder » Arts & Culture
feeds.description: Preparing a conscious community now and for the future. The Recorder is the fourth-oldest African American newspaper in the country, serving Indianapolis since 1895. Preparing a conscious community today and beyond.

feeds.title: South Shore Arts Blog
feeds.description: South Shore Arts has been serving Northwest Indiana for over 80 years. Please visit us soon at one of our community art centers in Munster and Hammond to discover the artist within you.

feeds.title: East Region Tourism IN Indiana » Art
Storytelling Arts of Indiana Blog
feeds.description: Storytelling Arts of Indiana is a non-profit that promotes the art of storytelling by creating opportunities in Indiana for diverse audiences of all ages to listen and share stories and by showcasing tellers who entertain and inspire.

feeds.title: Visit Indy Blog » Arts & Culture
feeds.description: As Visit Indy, it's our mission to enhance the quality of life in Indianapolis by optimizing visitor-related economic impact. And that job has never been more energizing or more rewarding than it is right now. As an unprecedented level of cooperation between business and government boosts Indianapolis to a completely new level, we're reveling in the opportunity to show our city off. Interested in connecting with Visit Indy?

feeds.title: Go SoIN Blog » Arts & Culture
feeds.description: Go SoIN are SoIN Tourism, helping visitors find fun things to see and do in Southern Indiana's Clark and Floyd Counties. Explore a wealth of information when it comes to planning your Southern Indiana vacation. Find upcoming event details, travel advice, lodging, and information.

feeds.title: Brown County Art Gallery Blog
feeds.description: Founded in 1926 by an early colony of impressionists artists, the Brown County Art Gallery has supported Indiana artists, past, present, and future for nearly 100 years. Their 15,000 square foot facility is home to 60 working artists as well as an important permanent collection of historic art.
